reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must accept FUNCTION CHAR followed by exactly one parenthesised integer argument-1, as an alphanumeric function-identifier wherever an identifier is permitted except as a receiving operand, with an optional reference-modifier, and refuse zero or two arguments, the bare name and an empty '( )'.

edition-consulted.switches: the D8 window: sig.IntroducedIn (85 on this row) against ctx.Edition.DialectLevel, COBOL1502 below it
construct function-empty-argument-list-2002: an empty '( )' after the name draws COBOL0900 below 2002 (the 1985 format braces argument-1 inside the parentheses)
construct RepositoryFunction2002: below 2002 a name written without FUNCTION is never read as a function (it binds as a data reference, COBOL1639); at 2023 it draws COBOL1543
FUNCTION is reserved at r85 (true at every edition)

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 an empty '( )' argument list is refused by COBOL0900 before the arity check and the keyword-omitted form is not a function reference; CHAR is alphanumeric, so it is an identifier anywhere at every edition and may be reference-modified. The arity check (COBOL1504) is the same code at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f34_02 and the RV witnesses exercise literal, identifier and expression arguments as MOVE senders; reference modification of the result, a relation operand, the receiving-operand refusal and the count refusals are not exercised

probes.printed: MOVE FUNCTION CHAR (N) N=66 -> [A]; CHAR (N + 1) (1:1) -> [B]; CHAR (67) into PIC XXX -> [B  ]; IF FUNCTION CHAR (66) = "A" -> CHARCMP A
probes.expected: ordinal 66 of the native sequence is 'A'; a reference-modifier is allowed on an alphanumeric function (§1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR2); one-character result padded

probes.printed: FUNCTION CHAR (65 66), bare CHAR and CHAR ( ) -> COBOL1504; ( ) also COBOL0900
MOVE C TO FUNCTION CHAR (66) -> COBOL5506 unexpected 'FUNCTION' (at 85 and 2023)
CHAR (1) = LOW-VALUE true; ORD (CHAR (256)) = 256; ORD (HIGH-VALUE) = 65536 (5536 in a 9(4)), so CHAR (256) is not HIGH-VALUE; same at --std 2023
probes.expected: implementor-defined native sequence (§1989:A.2.9.4 RV2); its size here is 65536 positions

probes.printed: --std 85: MOVE FUNCTION ACOS (X) TO R and MOVE FUNCTION VARIANCE (1 2) TO R -> COBOL0900 (numeric function-identifier as identifier operand requires COBOL-2002); FUNCTION ANNUITY (0.1 3) (1:2) -> COBOL1629; FUNCTION ATAN (LEADING) -> COBOL1638; ASIN (X) without FUNCTION -> COBOL1639 not defined; MOVE FUNCTION CHAR (66) TO C (1:1) accepted. --std 2023: the two MOVEs accepted, the rest refused (ASIN -> COBOL1543)
probes.expected: §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4 numeric function only in an arithmetic expression; SR2 reference-modifier only for alphanumeric functions; the 1985 format has no keyword-omitted form; a phrase word is no argument

reader.notes: Catalog row CHAR (Alphanumeric, Fixed 1..1, kind 'i', IntroducedIn 85, Length Fixed(1)); as an alphanumeric function it passes ScreenIdentifierPlacement at 85, and its result may be reference-modified. The native program collating sequence has 65536 positions, which is the implementor's choice under RV2 and outside this format row.
